openings.claim: Develop the surname system with a live, behind-desk exception slip: record household-name discrepancies and update an exception whenever its book moves. This addresses unreliable addresses; its benefit remains untested.
openings.delta: Retain divider cards, shelves and cart; replace the once-before-opening exception snapshot with updates tied to actual moves.
openings.prediction: If unreliable addresses drive delays, encounters with verified surname mappings and current locations should require fewer second searches and finish faster, including within the busy interval.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is queue congestion: even accurately located books will exceed two minutes mainly during the 25-minute burst, with little improvement from location corrections.
openings.defeat: A counterexample is continued second searches or unchanged delays despite verified household mappings and current exception locations; concentration among queued encounters would defeat the address-based explanation.
openings.probe: The existing clerk uses paper and the timing sheet for a bounded trial, recording address correctness, second searches and queue presence. Keep identities behind the desk, require claimant-to-hold verification before handoff, and stop preparation at ten clerk-minutes. Count preparation and reconciliation time explicitly.
assumptions: Fit evaluates the bounded probe; achieving 95% within two minutes and zero wrong-reader handoffs remains unproven.
The clerk can maintain exception updates during service; an adequate identity-verification procedure is not supplied.

openings.claim: New arrivals may be faster to retrieve on the existing cart than after alphabetic shelving; O4 defeats any universal claim that shelving necessarily accelerates retrieval.
openings.delta: Test whether retaining a bounded arrival cohort on the cart avoids address ambiguity without sacrificing prompt, correct pickup.
openings.prediction: For comparable arrival cohorts, cart retrieval remains faster while claimant verification prevents wrong-reader handoffs.
openings.rival_prediction: Sample selection is the nearest alternative: the ten cart pickups involved unusually small or easy cohorts; the advantage disappears as arrival volume or book size increases.
openings.defeat: Matched cohorts show slower cart retrieval, reduced correctness, or a cart capacity limit that prevents the proposed arrangement.
openings.probe: Use existing furniture and timing paper to compare naturally occurring cart and shelf pickups, recording arrival volume and book size. Bound preparation to ten clerk-minutes; treat unmatched comparisons as inconclusive.
assumptions: Fit evaluates observation only; routine cart retention is unproven.
Comparable cohorts and sufficient cart capacity are unknown.
